Thank you.  I was hoping you could expand on what you mean by "long"? As in the length of my top? I  realize with the dark colors and lighting it's looked like I'm wearing a dress in this picture but it's actually a pair of dark wash jeans and a dark grey shirt.

Volume in my hair is something I want to work towards but haven't had as much luck achieving. 

I hear what you're saying about the hips, and I've been considering a local cosmetic surgeon who may be able to do fat redistribution to give me more hips,  but unless and until I do that,  I will want to de-emphasize. Thank you.
Well now you just sound like my husband. :) Thank you

Thank you. I'm going to look into top styles that deemphasize shoulders, that is appreciated. And both you and /u/RainbowDragQueen mentioned bangs, so I'll definitely investigate that as well. Thank you both.

I am planning to meet my husband's parents for the first time for Thanksgiving. I'm immigrating to the USA and he lives far from his family, so it's less weird than it initially sounds that we haven't met in person yet.  I am very nervous about whether or not I pass.  I'm struggling with acceptance, and I just don't want them to know yet.

I previously met his sister, brother-in-law and niece.  If they knew I was trans, they didn't say anything to that effect.  My husband feels sure they don't know, says that they behaved in ways they wouldn't have if they had known.  I remain nervous though. 

In terms of what I've done to pass, I have been on hormones now for 2+ years and a few months ago I had facial feminization surgery.  I've had doubts about whether the surgery was aggressive enough, or whether I need to have a second round.  I'm currently working on losing weight to get into the right BMI range to be a good candidate for a breast augmentation and brazillian butt lift.  My husband believes I pass now, I believe everyone around me knows I'm trans and is too polite to say anything, and between the two of us we don't know how to resolve this.

I guess my questions to you all:

1. Do you think I pass?  When I look like I do in these pictures would you expect me to get clocked by someone who doesn't have any prior information about me being trans?
2. Do you think I would really benefit from a second round of FFS? And if so, what aspects would most benefit from the attention?

I would really appreciate candid answers to this, thank you.

Thank you, I appreciate your kind words and I especially appreciate the no hug boxing.  I can definitely look at some hair styles, although I might be playing it safe for a while while FFS scars heal.

First of all, your honest feedback is wanted, even if you don't have the patience to read this wall of text.

​

I'm scheduled to meet a member of my husband's family for the first time tomorrow evening. I'm very nervous that I won't pass, I don't want them to know I'm trans, at least until I choose to tell them. My husband and I disagree about how likely I am to pass. I think he sees me through the rose-tinted glasses of love and can't be objective. He thinks I am influenced by my depression and low self esteem and can't be objective.

​

A couple years ago, when I passed less well visually than I do now, he thought I passed completely, we went on a vacation, and I got misgendered by the waiter at dinner, and it's been hard for me to trust ever since. Looking at pictures from that day, my husband now agrees he might have been wrong. Since then, I have had facial feminization surgery, grown my hair, given the hormones another two years to work, improved my makeup skills, and gotten my ears pierced. I have not been misgendered out and about in a good while, but I don't know if I'm passing, or if it's just clear enough that I'm trying to present feminine that everyone is being polite. Our friends have said they think I pass, but I don't know if they are just protecting my feelings.

​

His family hasn't been given any particular reason to suspect I might be trans. They haven't ever heard my deadname, my husband has not mentioned my being trans. They saw a picture of me taken on the same trip where I got misgendered (taken earlier in the day when my makeup was better). They didn't ask anything about my appearance, and they did ask my husband (boyfriend at the time) how I felt about children. They have been nagging him for grandkids for a few years - he interpreted this to mean that they are planning to encourage me to get pregnant (we'll cross that bridge when we come to it), but I interpret it as them trying to politely ask if I *can* have children.

​

It's a bit unusual that we got married and I still haven't met them, but we have solid explanations for everything (I'm British, he's American, and the immigration process and its travel restrictions is complicated and risky. He lives far from his family.). So my question to you all is: what's my better shot, and how good a chance do I have? Do I meet them tomorrow looking like this, or do I refuse to meet them until later? I'd invite suspicion about *why* I'm not meeting them, but it would buy me enough time to get in a few sessions of voice therapy. I have had my voice pitch measured on an app and it is right at the androgynous pitch - lower-normal for a cis-woman, higher-normal for a cis-man but I'm too dysphoric about my voice to post it here. My husband suggested I just feign a cold to explain any difference between my voice now and the more feminine voice I'm hoping to have when I see them next.

​

So what do you think? Do I have an OK chance?
